option.counterfactual: Extremal graphs cannot always be assembled as a linear chain of blocks separated by bridges or articulation vertices; a more highly connected component is essential for some vertex counts.

belief.answer: For N=\binom n2, H=(n^{n-2})!, B=2^{N+n}, and \delta(x)=\lfloor1/(|x|+1)\rfloor, define A_b (0\le b<2^N) to be the symmetric zero-diagonal matrix whose upper-triangular entries, in lexicographic order, are the binary digits of b starting with the least significant digit. Put d_{b,i}=\sum_j(A_b)_{ij} and L_b=\operatorname{diag}(d_{b,1},\ldots,d_{b,n})-A_b. Write L^{[S]} for deletion of the rows and columns indexed by S, and set a_b=\det L_b^{[\{n\}]}, f_{b,uv}=\det L_b^{[\{u,v\}]}, q_b=a_b+\delta(a_b), and w_b=(1-\delta(a_b))\prod_{i=2}^n\delta(d_{b,i}-d_{b,1}). Then, throughout the stated domain, \boxed{\displaystyle t_n=\frac1H\left\lfloor\log_B\!\left(1+\sum_{b=0}^{2^N-1}w_b\sum_{1\le u<v\le n}B^{Hn d_{b,1}f_{b,uv}/q_b}\right)\right\rfloor}.

options.approach: Search higher-degree regular graphs at the smallest admissible vertex counts and compare their commute times with the best degree-3 and degree-4 constructions. Compute promising examples exactly using Laplacian minors.
